title: India's footballers lose 3-0 to New Zealand, ending tour with eight goals conceded
dek: All three goals in Christchurch came in the first half, three days after a 5-0 defeat in Auckland. It was India's seventh loss under coach Khalid Jamil this year, one report said.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India's men's football team lost 3-0 to New Zealand in an international friendly at One New Zealand Stadium in Christchurch on Sunday, finishing a two-match tour without scoring and having conceded eight goals.

New Zealand scored all three goals in a 21-minute spell in the first half. Defender Finn Surman headed in a corner from Callum McCowatt in the 22nd minute, James McGarry ran on to a pass from Owen Parker-Price to make it 2-0 in the 40th minute, and captain Chris Wood added a third three minutes later, the ball going in off his shin after a move involving Matthew Garbett and Jesse Randall, according to match reports.

The first match, in Auckland on Thursday, ended 5-0 to New Zealand, with Randall scoring twice, reports said.

## How India played

Coach Khalid Jamil made five changes to his starting line-up from the Auckland match and switched to a five-man defence. Ryan Williams captained the side for the first time, and Mehtab Singh took the armband when Williams was substituted. Goalkeeper Vishal Kaith made several saves in the first half, including one from a Wood header in the 44th minute, which kept the score from growing before half-time.

Jamil made three changes at the break, including handing a debut to goalkeeper Hrithik Tiwari, who made a number of saves in the second half. India's best chance came in the 81st minute, when Liston Colaco shot over from long range, and Bijoy Varghese cleared a shot off the line in the 86th minute to prevent a fourth goal.

The defeat was India's seventh under Jamil in 2026, one report said. New Zealand were coached by Darren Bazeley.

## Background

The November window was India's chance to test themselves against stronger opposition away from home. New Zealand, who play in the Oceania confederation, qualified for this year's FIFA World Cup in North America; India did not. Jamil, who took charge in 2025 after a long career coaching Indian clubs, used the two matches to try several players, including a debutant goalkeeper.

The tour ran alongside the SAFF Championship in Dhaka, where a separate India side beat Pakistan 3-2 in a group match on 5 November, according to reports.

## What happens next

One report said India's SAFF Championship side meets Pakistan in the final in Dhaka on Tuesday, 17 November, at 7:30 pm IST; the tournament organisers' schedule could not be independently checked. The players on the New Zealand tour return to their clubs for the Indian Super League.
